descriptors.concept_name: Charging Provision and Scope of Capital Gains
descriptors.definition: Profits and gains arising from the transfer of a capital asset effected in a tax year are chargeable to income-tax under the head Capital Gains and deemed as income of that specific year. The core elements driving this charge are the identification of a valid capital asset and a recognized transfer.
inclusion: Property of any kind held by an assessee
Securities held by specified Foreign Institutional Investors or investment funds
Unit linked insurance policies without specific exemptions
exclusion: Stock-in-trade held for business or profession
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between items held as business stock-in-trade versus items held as personal investments based on the manner of holding rather than the inherent nature of the asset.

descriptors.definition: A capital asset encompasses property of any kind held by an assessee alongside specific institutional securities and non-exempt unit linked insurance policies, irrespective of business connection. Stock-in-trade, consumable stores, and raw materials held for business are generally excluded from this definition.
inclusion: Assessee-held property connected or unconnected with business
Securities held by qualified Foreign Institutional Investors and investment funds
Non-exempt unit linked insurance policies
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes asset classification purely by the holding intent and manner, making identical physical property either a capital asset under investment or stock-in-trade under trading.

descriptors.concept_name: Short Term and Long Term Capital Assets
descriptors.definition: Capital assets are classified based on their holding period preceding transfer into short-term or long-term categories, generally utilizing a twenty-four-month threshold unless specific assets mandate a shorter twelve-month or overriding short-term treatment. Equity-oriented funds and specific financial instruments maintain distinct percentage thresholds for classification.
inclusion: Assets held for more than twenty-four months as long-term
Listed securities, units of UTI, equity-oriented funds, and zero coupon bonds held for more than twelve months as long-term
Specific specified mutual funds, market-linked debentures, and unlisted bonds treated strictly as short-term
exclusion: Assets not meeting the prescribed holding duration criteria for long-term status
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates standard assets requiring a 24-month holding period from listed financial securities requiring a 12-month period and statutory instruments forcing short-term treatment irrespective of duration.

descriptors.definition: Transfer encompasses an inclusive range of transactions regarding capital assets, including sales, exchanges, relinquishments, extinguishment of rights, and compulsory acquisitions. It also covers asset conversions to stock-in-trade, zero coupon bond maturities, and arrangements enabling immovable property enjoyment.
inclusion: Sale, exchange, or relinquishment of an asset
Conversion of capital assets into business stock-in-trade
Granting possession of immovable property under part-performance contracts
exclusion: Transactions explicitly shielded from transfer status under statutory exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard conveyances from constructive transfers such as part-performance possession, corporate conversions, and bond maturities that lack traditional registered deeds.

descriptors.definition: Capital gains are chargeable as income in the specific tax year when the actual sale or transfer takes place rather than the date of an initial agreement to sell. Insurance receipts from insurers due to asset destruction from natural convulsions, riots, or accidents are similarly chargeable under this head.
instrument_references: Principal CIT v. Gujarat State Fertilizers and Chemicals Limited
inclusion: Profits from asset transfers effected in the tax year
Insurance compensation received for asset destruction via natural calamities, riots, or explosions
exclusion: Gains governed by specific statutory exemptions outside the charging provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes the exact legal transfer date establishing tax year liability from preliminary execution milestones like sale agreements.

descriptors.concept_name: Capital Gains on Distribution of Assets by Companies in Liquidation
descriptors.definition: Asset distributions by a liquidated company to its shareholders are not treated as transfers at the company level, while shareholders face capital gains tax based on the market value of received assets minus accumulated profit components. Portions of distributions attributable to accumulated profits are treated separately as dividend income under other income sources.
inclusion: Shareholder capital gains on money or assets received during company liquidation
Fair market value adoption as cost of acquisition for subsequent asset sales by shareholders
exclusion: Distribution events treated as company transfers when liquidators sell assets directly prior to distribution
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes company-level exemption from asset distribution against shareholder-level taxation which splits distributions into deemed dividends and capital gains.

descriptors.concept_name: Capital Gains on Buyback of Shares or Other Securities
descriptors.definition: Consideration received from a company for the buyback of its shares or specified securities is chargeable as capital gains calculated as the difference between consideration and acquisition cost. Promoters face additional income tax and flat surcharges on such capital gains alongside standard tax rates.
inclusion: Consideration received by shareholders on share and security buybacks
Additional tax liabilities for promoters on specific short-term and long-term capital gains
exclusion: Standard non-promoter share transfers governed strictly by general capital gain rates without additional promoter surcharges
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard shareholder tax treatment on buybacks from promoter-specific tax obligations that impose additional tier-based levies and flat surcharges.

descriptors.definition: Amalgamation denotes the merger of one or more companies into another company where all properties and liabilities transfer to the amalgamated entity and specified majority shareholders transition their holdings. Demerger involves the transfer of undertaking units pursuant to a scheme of arrangement under company law preserving asset and liability continuity.
inclusion: Mergers involving complete property and liability absorption
Demerger schemes transferring undertakings to resulting companies
exclusion: Asset purchases or winding-up distributions that fail to meet statutory merger continuity thresholds
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes full corporate amalgamation combining total entities from demerger frameworks transferring specific undertakings while keeping the originating company intact.

descriptors.definition: Specific statutory provisions ensure certain structural reorganizations and family partitions are not treated as transfers for capital gains purposes. These exemptions apply to conditions involving Hindu Undivided Family partitions, gifts, trusts, and qualifying holding-subsidiary or amalgamation transfers.
inclusion: Distributions upon total or partial partition of a Hindu Undivided Family
Transfers under a will, gift, or irrevocable trust
Qualifying transfers between Indian holding and wholly owned subsidiary companies
exclusion: Transfers involving stock-in-trade under holding-subsidiary arrangements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes regular taxable asset transfers from statutory non-transfer events like corporate amalgamations and family gifts that defer tax realization.

descriptors.concept_name: Withdrawal of Exemption in Certain Cases
descriptors.definition: Exemptions granted for holding-subsidiary company asset transfers are withdrawn if the transferee converts the asset into stock-in-trade or the parent company ceases to hold the entire share capital within eight years. Similar clawback provisions apply to failed conditions following firm successions or company-to-LLP conversions.
inclusion: Exemption revocations when transferee converts assets to stock-in-trade within eight years
Deemed capital gains income realization upon parent company shareholding dilution
exclusion: Compliant transfers maintaining holding structures and asset capitalization beyond the statutory eight-year window
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes initial tax-free restructuring transfers from subsequent taxable events triggered by post-transfer statutory condition breaches.

descriptors.concept_name: Mode of Computation of Capital Gains
descriptors.definition: Capital gains income is computed by deducting transfer-related expenditures and the cost of acquisition or improvement from the full value of consideration. For specific long-term capital assets acquired before a designated date by resident individuals or Hindu Undivided Families, tax adjustments ignore excess tax computed without indexation benefits.
inclusion: Deductions for exclusive transfer expenditures like brokerage and stamp duty
Cost inflation index applications for eligible resident individuals and Hindu Undivided Families
exclusion: Indexation benefits when computing gross total income figures under the capital gains head
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes raw capital gains income computation from specialized tax-payable computations that incorporate indexation comparison formulas for resident individuals and Hindu Undivided Families.

descriptors.concept_name: Ascertainment of Cost in Specified Circumstances
descriptors.definition: When an assessee acquires a capital asset through non-purchase methods such as gifts, succession, company liquidation, or structural amalgamations, the cost of acquisition is deemed as the cost incurred by the previous owner. Transferees in these specified circumstances are also permitted to include the previous owner's holding period for classification purposes.
inclusion: Asset costs derived from the last previous owner under gifts, wills, and successions
Inclusion of previous owner holding periods for short-term and long-term asset determination
exclusion: Direct market purchases where the acquirer establishes an independent original purchase cost
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct purchase cost accounting from derivative cost tracking where asset ownership changes via inheritance, restructuring, or statutory distribution without fresh market acquisition.
